This vignette summarises the principal PscanR functions for motif enrichment
analysis in promoter sequences. The package reference manual provides complete
argument descriptions and examples.

<hr />

# Table 1: Motif enrichment analysis and input preparation

<table style="border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%;">
    <thead>
    <tr>
        <th style="width:20%; border-bottom: 2px solid #ccc;">Function</th>
        <th style="width:80%; border-bottom: 2px solid #ccc;">Description</th>
    </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;"><code>pscan()</code></td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Computes the best match to each motif in each promoter and tests motif
    enrichment against the supplied background score distributions.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    <code>pscan_fullBG()</code>
</td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Retrieves stored motif hits for foreground identifiers from a full
    background and calculates enrichment without rescanning the DNA sequences.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;"><code>pscan_filtered()</code></td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Selects promoters whose best match to a specified motif meets a threshold
    defined from its background distribution, then scans the selected promoters
    against the supplied motif collection.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;"><code>ps_select_promoters()</code></td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Selects one promoter per mapped gene from supplied sequences and annotation,
    using transcript preferences or rules appropriate to the identifier scheme.
    Reports the scheme and the reason for each selection.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;"><code>ps_selection_summary()</code></td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Summarises a mapping produced by <code>ps_select_promoters()</code>, including
    identifier schemes, selection rules, genes with multiple candidates, and
    selections requiring a tie-breaking rule after ranking.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td><code>ps_load_select_transcripts()</code></td>
        <td>
    Downloads and caches human hg38 MANE Select and RefSeq Select metadata from
    UCSC for use with <code>ps_select_promoters()</code>. Other organisms require
    an appropriate user-supplied selection table or representative selection.
</td>
    </tr>
    </tbody>
</table>

<hr />

# Table 2: Background construction

A background describes the distribution of best motif scores across a defined
reference set of promoters. A standard background stores the number of
promoters, mean score, and score standard deviation for each motif; a full
background also retains the individual hits. Foreground and background must
use matching promoter definitions and motif matrices.

<table style="border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%;">
    <thead>
    <tr>
        <th style="width:30%; border-bottom: 2px solid #ccc;">Function</th>
        <th style="width:70%; border-bottom: 2px solid #ccc;">Description</th>
    </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
            <code>ps_build_bg()</code>
        </td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Scans the supplied reference sequences and computes background statistics
    for each motif after sequence filtering and deduplication.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    <code>generate_psmatrixlist_from_background()</code>
</td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Retrieves a precomputed background and associates its statistics with the
    matching motif matrices in a <code>PSMatrixList</code>.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    <code>get_availableBG()</code>
</td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Displays the names of all available precomputed backgrounds, with options to
    filter by keywords.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;"><code>ps_retrieve_bg_from_file()</code></td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Reads a background text file and associates the stored size, mean score,
    and standard deviation with the supplied motif matrices by identifier.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;"><code>ps_build_bg_from_table()</code></td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Associates background parameters held in a <code>data.frame</code> with a list of position frequency matrices and returns the result as a <code>PSMatrixList</code>.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;"><code>ps_get_bg_table()</code></td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Extracts the background statistics (size, mean and standard deviation) from a <code>PSMatrixList</code> as a <code>data.frame</code>, which is the inverse of <code>ps_build_bg_from_table()</code>.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;"><code>ps_write_bg_to_file()</code></td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Writes the background statistics of a <code>PSMatrixList</code> to a text file, in the format <code>ps_retrieve_bg_from_file()</code> reads back.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;"><code>ps_build_bg(fullBG = TRUE)</code></td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Builds a full background containing summary statistics and the best hit's
    score, position, strand, and matched oligonucleotide for each retained
    promoter and motif. Full backgrounds require substantially more storage;
    the package includes small demonstration objects.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;"><code>pscan_fullBG()</code></td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Uses foreground transcript identifiers to retrieve hits stored in a full
    background. Reusing these hits reduces computation for repeated analyses
    against the same reference set.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td><code>transcriptIDLegend()</code></td>
        <td>
    Retrieves the mapping from original sequence names to representatives
    retained after deduplication. This allows <code>pscan_fullBG()</code> to
    resolve identifiers associated with identical promoter sequences.
</td>
    </tr>
    </tbody>
</table>

<hr />

# Table 3: Result summaries and visualisation

<table style="border-collapse: collapse; width: 100%;">
    <thead>
    <tr>
        <th style="width:25%; border-bottom: 2px solid #ccc;">Function</th>
        <th style="width:85%; border-bottom: 2px solid #ccc;">Description</th>
    </tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    <code>ps_results_table()</code>
</td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Returns motif-level results ordered by increasing p-value, with decreasing
    z-score used to resolve ties. Motifs can be selected using a specified
    false discovery rate (FDR) threshold.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
            <code>ps_z_table()</code>
        </td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Returns a matrix of standardised best-hit scores, with promoters as rows
    and motifs as columns, from a <code>PSMatrixList</code>.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    <code>ps_zscore_heatmap()</code>
</td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Displays a heatmap of per-promoter motif z-scores after motif selection by
    FDR. By default, rows are scaled and both axes are clustered using
    correlation distances; the cells are not pairwise correlation coefficients.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    <code>ps_hitpos_map()</code>
</td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
        Displays the position of each promoter's best motif match as a heatmap
        to compare positional patterns across motifs.
        </td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    <code>ps_density_plot()</code>
</td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
        Estimates the positional density of a motif's best hits, optionally
        restricted by a score threshold. A supplied promoter window enables
        boundary correction, and optional bins show a histogram on the same
        density scale.
        </td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;"><code>ps_hit_score_plot()</code></td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Plots best-hit score against position for each promoter, allowing joint
    assessment of match strength and positional concentration.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;"><code>ps_motif_barplot()</code></td>
        <td style="border-bottom: 1px solid #ddd;">
    Displays the highest-ranked motifs as horizontal bars, optionally coloured
    by a grouping such as transcription factor structural class.
</td>
    </tr>
    <tr>
        <td><code>ps_motif_class()</code></td>
        <td>
    Extracts the transcription factor structural class associated with each
    motif, for example <code>"Basic leucine zipper factors (bZIP)"</code>, for
    annotation or grouping in <code>ps_motif_barplot()</code>.
</td>
    </tr>
    </tbody>
</table>
